title: Hermetic scratch-git helper and test git discipline
summary: Every test that builds a throwaway repository now goes through one shared helper, `scratch_git`, which runs git from an empty environment against a directory confined to the temp root, so no inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, global config or hook identity can redirect it. Production code gains a small split in `git.rs` (`INDEX_FILE_VAR`, `scrub_locating_git_env`) reused by `assets.rs` and `moon.rs`, and a new tree-sitter-based test fails the build if any test code starts git itself or names a repository-locating variable.

nodes.label: scratch_git helper
nodes.subtitle: run / ok / init / init_bare
nodes.summary: Runs `git -C dir` with `env_clear()`, an empty HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and `LC_ALL=C`, after resolving `dir` and refusing anything outside the temp root. `init` also sets a fixed identity and disables commit signing.

nodes.label: confine_to_temp_root
nodes.subtitle: fn confine_to_temp_root(dir: &Path) -> PathBuf
nodes.summary: Rejects relative paths and `..` segments, then canonicalises the nearest existing parent and asserts the result starts with the canonical temp root.

nodes.label: empty_home
nodes.subtitle: fn empty_home() -> PathBuf
nodes.summary: A shared empty folder under the temp root used as HOME/USERPROFILE/XDG_CONFIG_HOME so no `~/.gitconfig` is read.

nodes.label: tests/common/mod.rs
nodes.subtitle: TempRepo, BareRepo, git_with_hook_env
nodes.summary: Re-exports `scratch_git` and rewrites `TempRepo::new`, `BareRepo::new` and `git_with_hook_env` to call it, keeping the PATH/HOME overrides as explicit env entries.

nodes.label: Unit-test modules
nodes.subtitle: builder, checkpoint, config, clean_copy, changeset_tests, git
nodes.summary: In-crate `#[cfg(test)]` modules that used to hand-roll `git init`/`git config`/`git commit` now call `crate::scratch_git`, wired in through a `#[path]` module in lib.rs.

nodes.label: Integration tests
nodes.subtitle: assets_publish, hooks_install, moon_adapter, review_run, real_hook_runs
nodes.summary: Each test file drops its own `Command::new("git")` plumbing and calls `common::scratch_git::run`/`ok`/`init`/`init_bare`. `git_env_hermetic.rs` is renamed to `real_hook_runs.rs` and loses its nested-cargo sentinel tests.

nodes.label: scratch_git.rs tests
nodes.subtitle: tests/scratch_git.rs
nodes.summary: Proves the helper's contract: no global config leaks in, a triggered hook sees only the cleared environment, and out-of-temp or relative directories panic.

nodes.label: test_git_discipline
nodes.subtitle: tree-sitter scan of test code
nodes.summary: Parses every `.rs` under `crates/*/src` and `crates/*/tests`, and in test code refuses `Command::new("git")` and string literals naming `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or `GIT_COMMON_DIR`. The helper and the rule itself are exempt.

nodes.label: git.rs
nodes.subtitle: scrub_git_env_for_dir, run, merge_base
nodes.summary: Introduces `INDEX_FILE_VAR` and `scrub_locating_git_env`, routes `scrub_with_index` through the latter, and makes `merge_base` scrub the environment like every other git call.

nodes.label: scrub_locating_git_env
nodes.subtitle: fn scrub_locating_git_env(command: &mut Command)
nodes.summary: Removes only the `GIT_*` variables that name which repository to use, leaving `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and everything else alone — the variant a child that runs git itself needs.

nodes.label: INDEX_FILE_VAR
nodes.subtitle: pub(crate) const INDEX_FILE_VAR: &str
nodes.summary: Names `GIT_INDEX_FILE` once so no test code spells the variable out, which is what the discipline guard enforces.

nodes.label: assets::run_git
nodes.subtitle: fn run_git(dir, args)
nodes.summary: Now scrubs the git environment for the target directory before running, so asset publishing cannot be redirected by an inherited `GIT_DIR`.

nodes.label: moon::strip_inherited_moon_vars
nodes.subtitle: fn strip_inherited_moon_vars(command)
nodes.summary: Also calls `scrub_locating_git_env`, so a nested moon finds its repository from its working directory rather than a caller's `GIT_DIR`.
